newsitem.title: CHINA: China approves 38 firms to be listed abroad.
newsitem.headline: China approves 38 firms to be listed abroad.

text.p: China has approved 38 companies for listing their shares on stock markets abroad, the official Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

Xinhua said the Securities Commission under the State Council had approved the Beijing Yanshan Petrochemical Co and China Great Wall Computer Group Co among 38 firms on the long-awaited list of China's fourth such batch.
The announcement did not specify on which stock markets the government planned to list the latest batch of firms to win approval to raise funds abroad.
However, most were expected to be listed as H shares on the Hong Kong stock market, analysts said.

"The fourth batch of enterprises are more representative, whether from the point of view of geographical location or industrial sector," Xinhua said, quoting a spokesman for the China Securities Regulatory Commission, China's top watchdog.
"They can better reflect the potential growth and overall development level of China's economy," it said.

The list included enterprises based in the more developed southern and eastern coastal regions, firms from China's traditional heavy industrial base in the northeast and the developing central and western areas, Xinhua said.

The industries represented ranged from electricity, power, communications, metallurgy, non-ferrous metals and building materials, to chemicals, machinery and electronics as well as pharmaceuticals and electrical appliances, it said.

Among best-known firms were the Three Nine Pharmaceutical Co Ltd, the Guangzhou-based giant run by the People's Liberation Army, and the China World Trade Centre that runs a hotel and office complex in central Beijing.
Others were the Angang Sanxin Co Ltd, the profitable arm of giant steel-maker Anshan Steel in northeast Liaoning province, and Tianjin Motor Co, which turns out a popular low-cost car.
Also included were Shanghai Electric Power Co Ltd, power investment arm of the Shanghai government, and Wuhan Yangluo Electric Power Co Ltd, in which the New York-listed Huaneng Group has a stake.
Other power firms were Guizhou Wujiang Hydroelectric (Group) Co Ltd, Jilin Electric Power Co Ltd, Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co Ltd and the Anhui Xinji Power Development Co Ltd.
Also listed is the China Aquatic Products Co.
Road firms were Jiangsu Ninghu Expressway Co Ltd, Zhejiang Hangyong Expressway Co Ltd and Chengyu Expressway Co Ltd.
Metallurgical firms included the Chongqing Steel (Group) Co Ltd, Panzhihua Steel (Group) Co, as well as the Jiangxi Copper Co and Qinghai Aluminium Co Ltd.
Chemical firms included Beijing Yanshan Petrochemical Co, Panjin Ethylene Enterprise Co, Sichuan Chuanhua Group Co, a large fertiliser maker, and Jinan Chemical Fibre Co.
Two cement firms are Anhui Ningguo Cement Plant and Hebei Taihang Cement Co. Also listed is the Number One Tractor Construction and Machinery Group.
Henan Anyang Colour Television Tube Co Ltd and Rainbow Screen Co Ltd were on the list.
Electronics makers include Qingdao Aucma Electrical Appliances Co that makes freezers and dishwashers, and Jiangxi Huayi Compressor Co Ltd.
Pharmaceuticals firms were Huabei Pharmaceuticals Group Co Ltd, Harbin Pharmaceuticals Co Ltd and Guangzhou Pharmaceuticals Group Co Ltd.

Property developer Beijing North Star Development Co was included as well as China Huandao (Group) Co, the Yunnan Travel Group Co Ltd, China Merchants Shekou Industrial Zone Co Ltd and the China Aerospace Technology Import Export Co (Shenzhen).

The regulatory commission said that of the 38 firms in the first three batches, 26 had so far been listed and of these 24 were listed in Hong Kong. The latest 38 do not include the 12 from earlier batches that have yet to obtain a listing, it said.

In previous batches, those that have listed have raised the equivalent of $4.9 billion and China's three years of listing firms abroad demonstrated that state firms had successfully listed their shares outside the country, it said.

This had been beneficial to their opening up new channels to foreign capital, it said. It had also been beneficial to strengthening the management of these companies and spurring the development of China's securities industry, it said.
